Every shadow seemed to hide a secret from her past. The floorboards groaned beneath her heavy boots as she walked. A cold breeze swept through the empty and abandoned hallway. She remembered the stories her grandmother told about this place. They said a ghost wandered these rooms looking for peace. She did not believe in spirits or things beyond death. However, the chilling atmosphere made her doubt her own logic.

She pushed the heavy oak door to reveal a library. Books lined the tall walls from the floor to ceiling. A single candle flickered on the large mahogany reading desk. Who could have lit that candle in this forgotten house? She approached the desk with a steady but cautious stride. An open journal lay beside the small and melting wax. The dark ink was still wet in the dim glow. She leaned close to read the hastily written messy text. It said someone was waiting for her in the basement. Her heart began to beat faster inside her tight chest.

She stepped away to face the dark, silent, empty hall. The basement door waited at the far end of it. She walked toward it while holding her small silver light. It pointed a bony finger directly at her trembling face. The creature spoke softly, telling her to take its place. She shook her head violently and backed away in fear. There was no way she would stay in this tomb.

It knew that she could never truly escape this curse. She reached the top of the stairs and pushed forward. The hallway looked completely different now that she was back. The walls were covered in thick and pulsing red vines. The door to the outside world was now completely gone. She dropped to her knees and stared at the bricks. A deep realization washed over her tired and broken mind.

She was trapped inside the dark house for all eternity. The journal warned her about her dark and cruel fate. She should have listened to the old and spooky stories. Now she would become the very ghost that haunted others. Tears streamed down her pale cheeks as she accepted reality. The house groaned happily, welcoming its newest and permanent guest. Only her small silver flashlight remained on the dusty floor.
